A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NurValues. Their main texts, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 23 LLMs, prompting experiments, error analyses and statistical comparisons on the nursing benchmark.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds human evaluations, bootstrap analyses, alternative-generator tests, prompt steering and out-of-domain demonstrations.

M1.justification: The core construction procedure remains expert annotation, counterfactual polarity reversal and adversarial dialogue generation. The newly disclosed generation prompt documents that procedure; alternative generators and steering methods are additional experimental treatments, not a replacement benchmark-construction method.

E1.justification: Appendix O newly uses medical-safety examples from MedSafetyBench and general-value examples from ValueBench as in-context demonstrations. The original nursing cases, Chinese/English coverage, five values and Easy/Hard tasks remain unchanged. Alternative-generator datasets retain the underlying clinical cases.

E2.justification: The main 23-model roster is unchanged, but v2 adds two human nurses as reference comparators against Claude 3.5 and 3.7 Sonnet (Table 4). It also compares ordinary prompting with DailyDilemma-style steering (Table 23) and introduces GPT-4o into few-shot comparisons (Table 24). These substantially extend the comparison framework beyond v1's model and prompting comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include 100 label-balanced cases per difficulty level for nurse testing, 200 pairs for human topic-consistency assessment, controlled generator substitutions, steering instructions and six-shot source comparisons. Appendix M adds precision, recall and complete confusion counts. The reported Hard-Level prompt now explicitly targets the initial case rather than behavior throughout the dialogue, and Appendix E revises API/local-deployment assignments; these documentation changes do not establish that the retained main experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds human checks of dialogue fidelity, generator-dependence tests, Justice sample-size robustness analysis, GPT-4o-versus-Claude error cases, steerability tests and demonstration-source sensitivity analysis. Conversely, v1's nursing-behavior distribution and linguistic-complexity analyses are removed. The medical-versus-base-model analysis is retained in Appendix G, not newly added.

E5.justification: V1 already reports McNemar tests, annotation agreement and dispersion of topic-similarity scores. V2 additionally resamples existing predictions 2,000 times using 74-instance samples across value dimensions, reporting bootstrap means, standard deviations and significance findings in Appendix F.1 and Tables 11–12. These are bootstrap repetitions, not 2,000 independent model runs.

E6.justification: The original main, per-value, ICL, error-count and McNemar results are retained. Substantial new results include human comparisons, generator variants, steering and source-dependent six-shot performance: GPT-4o's Hard-Level Ma-F1 is 68.46 with NurValues demonstrations, 58.35 with MedSafetyBench and 13.71 with ValueBench. New Table 21 also reports some conflicting repeated values: HuatuoGPT-o1-72B's Hard-Level F1 is 0.34 there, whereas v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 1 report 3.38.

T1.justification: Neither version presents a formal theoretical or proof contribution. The conceptual nursing-value definitions retain their meaning; the added bootstrap procedures and empirical metrics do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the first real-world nursing-value benchmark, its five dimensions and two difficulty levels, and the 23-model evaluation. V2 adds a more specific claim of relevance to LLM-mediated nurse–patient conflicts and a conclusion that LLMs lag behind human nurses on Hard-Level tasks. The principal benchmark and model-ranking claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning reasoning-model limitations, clinical consequences of false positives versus false negatives, resistance to value steering, generator independence and demonstration relevance. It interprets bootstrapping as excluding small-sample variability as the explanation for Justice difficulty. It also removes v1's explicit limitations concerning synthetic-dialogue realism, translation shifts and reliance on ICL, although concrete dataset defects remain acknowledged in the case study.

D1.justification: V2 supplies dated model identifiers, the adversarial-generation and topic-consistency prompts, human-evaluation instructions and value-steering system prompts. Appendix E revises implementation assignments while retaining the hardware description. The advertised code/data access location changes from Hugging Face to GitHub. Together these substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing a changed underlying construction method.

R1.justification: The introduction newly positions NurValues around patient trust and nurse–patient conflict, supported by additional clinical literature. Appendix B expands discussion to Utility Engineering, Values in the Wild, MoralBench, LitmusValues/AIRiskDilemmas and DailyDilemmas. The benchmark-comparison table is substantively rebuilt around value benchmarks, replacing the earlier mixed medical/general benchmark comparison.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around clinical conflict. Main-text organization changes through new human-testing and generator-robustness sections, relocation of domain-fine-tuning analysis to the appendix, and consolidation of limitations into the conclusion. The appendices are expanded and reorganized, alongside smaller language corrections.

P2.justification: V2 adds an illustrated clinical-conflict figure, redraws the construction pipeline and combines value-distribution and human/LLM consistency plots. It removes the hospital-photo panel and linguistic-feature table, adds multiple experimental tables, replaces the prompt graphic with text boxes, and relocates/reformats the Hard-Level McNemar matrix. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Human validation, alternative-generator controls, bootstrap reporting and explicit prompts make benchmark validity and reproducibility more assessable than in v1. The net gain is limited by removed realism/translation caveats, inconsistent repeated metrics in Tables 1 and 21, and an overly broad human-superiority conclusion: Table 4 shows Claude 3.5 Sonnet matching the nurses' mean Hard-Level Ma-F1 of 90.96. The additions improve the evidence, but do not fully resolve its interpretive and reporting weaknesses.
